Brand guidelines · Vol. 01

Two names.
One light.
Made in gold.

A small book of rules for a brand that turns what you mean into something worn.

ForLiNora Jewels
EditionOctober 2026
ByIntroducing Mo
Scroll
I. The name

Li+Nora

LiNora began as two names held together: Lina and Noor. Noor means light, and light is what gold does best, especially against deep cedar green.

The mark keeps both. An L and an N joined by one sweeping line, with a single stone set above. That line is the brand. It is what a gift does between two people.

What we sellBrazilian gold,
made personal.
What we meanA letter, a name,
a date someone keeps.
II. The line

Say it in gold.

When words run thin,
let gold begin.

Our signature for every box, card and caption. It makes the piece the message. You don't need the perfect sentence. Their initial, close to the heart, says it for you.

III. The mark

Three forms,
one signature.

Primary logo
Monogram
Wordmark
xx

Give it room.

Keep clear space on every side equal to x, the height of the stone above the N. Nothing enters that field: no text, no edge, no other logo.

Never too small.

Two colours only.

Cedar on light grounds, Linen on dark ones. For foil and engraving, the mark may be struck in gold.

Don't

Stretch, squeeze or rotate it.

Don't

Recolour it outside the palette.

Don't

Add shadows, glows or bevels.

Don't

Set it on a busy image.

VI. Mood

Soft light. Bare skin.
Real stone.

LiNora should feel like a quiet afternoon, not a jewellery counter. Natural textures, warm skin, one piece at a time. Gold is always the brightest thing in the frame.

Their name, their letter, their line.
Kept in gold, kept in time.

Small enough to hold,
big enough to be told.

Light

Daylight, diffused.

Window light or a soft box. No hard flash, no glare on the metal.

Ground

Things from the earth.

Travertine, linen, paper, petals, shells. Never glossy acrylic.

Skin

Close and warm.

Collarbones, wrists, fingers. Natural nails. Real texture left in.

Grade

Faded, never flat.

Lift the blacks, cool nothing, pull saturation back. Let the gold stay warm.

After dark

Cedar
& gold.

When the lights go low,
let the gold show.

Cedar can carry a whole surface: boxes, pouches, evening campaigns, the last frame of a reel. Text stays light and short on it; detailed information always sits on Chalk.

VII. In motion

Slow. Close.
Warm.

Reels move like the jewellery does: gently. Cut on a gesture, hold on the gold, end on the mark.

OpenA hand, a clasp, a letter catching light.
MiddleThe piece on skin. Two or three cuts, no more.
CloseMonogram in Linen, "Say it in gold."
SoundSoft and instrumental. Nothing that shouts over the gold.
VIII. Voice

Say less.
Mean more.

Brief

Few words, well chosen.

One line beats a paragraph. If gold can say it, we don't have to.

Warm

Talk to the giver.

Most pieces are bought for someone else. Speak to the person choosing, and the person they love.

Lyrical

A rhyme, when it's a gift.

Couplets belong on cards, boxes and seasonal moments. Product captions stay plain and clear.
